summary: Different ways to say "Do you have motion sickness medicine?" in Vietnam, with the safe phrase, reusable pieces, and nearby next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when travel motion is the problem and you want the medicine, not a doctor. Useful for buses, ferries, and mountain travel. Start with the full phrase, then use the nearby rows when the conversation needs one more step.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Có thuốc say xe không? is the safest default for "Do you have motion sickness medicine?". Use this when travel motion is the problem and you want the medicine, not a doctor. Say it slowly, then point, show your phone, or hold up the item if the other person needs more context.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Health phrases need to be simple because the other person may need to act quickly or ask a follow-up.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when travel motion is the problem and you want the medicine, not a doctor. Use it in doctors, pharmacies, symptoms, and medication when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: Do not soften urgent medical needs too much. Clear and direct is safer.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Show the symptom, medication, or affected area when possible. It gives the helper something concrete.
